name: Kathmandu
blurb: Nepal's capital and the starting point for most treks. Permits, gear rental, cash and last-minute supplies are all concentrated in and around Thamel.
tip: Sort permits and cash here; ATMs become scarce and unreliable once you leave the city.

name: Pokhara
blurb: The lakeside city below the Annapurna range and the hub for every trek in Annapurna and Mustang. Lakeside has gear shops, a permit office and frequent transport to the trailheads.
tip: The ACAP and TIMS counter is at the Nepal Tourism Board office in Damside.

name: Besisahar
blurb: District town of Lamjung and the traditional start of the Annapurna Circuit. Buses from Kathmandu and Pokhara stop here; jeeps continue up the Marsyangdi valley.

name: Dharapani
blurb: A junction village in the Marsyangdi gorge where the trail from the Larkya La and Manaslu meets the Annapurna Circuit. Permits are checked here.

name: Beni
blurb: Myagdi's district town at the meeting of the Kali Gandaki and Myagdi rivers. Roads branch north to Jomsom and west toward the Dhaulagiri approach.

name: Tatopani
blurb: A warm, low village on the Kali Gandaki named for its riverside hot springs. It links the Jomsom road with the climb to Ghorepani.

name: Marpha
blurb: A whitewashed Thakali village of flagstone lanes south of Jomsom, known for its apple orchards and a hillside monastery.

name: Jomsom
blurb: The windy administrative town of Mustang with an airstrip, banks and a permit checkpoint. Flights run in the early morning before the valley wind picks up.

name: Kagbeni
blurb: A mud-walled village at the confluence below Muktinath and the checkpoint where the Upper Mustang restricted area begins.

name: Muktinath
blurb: A pilgrimage site sacred to Hindus and Buddhists at the foot of the Thorong La. Lodges cluster in Ranipauwa, a short walk below the temple.
